correctness.rationale: Evans–Fuchs exact restricted p-map identity was checked in its original full text. For \(f_0\ne0\), the canonical cyclic vector makes the minimal polynomial degree p; the coefficient \([x^{p-1}]f^{p-1}\) is affine in \(f_{p-1}\) with slope \(-f_0^{p-2}\). For \(f_0=0,f_1\ne0\), p distinct diagonal eigenvalues give the extra split-semisimple counts. Frobenius multiplies roots of \(T^{p-1}-\lambda\) by \(\lambda^{(q-1)/(p-1)}\), establishing equal factor degrees. For \(k\ge2\), every power has rank max(p−1−h(k−1),0) by nonzero leading coefficients, proving the Jordan partition. Exact counts sum to \(q^p\). The standalone checker was replayed on three exhaustive finite fields and 900 samples at \(p=7\); all pass. Finite checks do not substitute for uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The 2001 scalar p-map theorem, 2014 geometric regularity theory, 2013 nilpotent Lie-commuting varieties, and two closely related published finite Witt counting results were compared by objects, operators, parameters and implication. The complete all-extension finite-field natural-action rational canonical type multiplicities and Frobenius splitting refinement are not explicitly covered by the inspected results; all older ingredients are credited. See four detailed named comparisons and residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-field arithmetic Jordan census may exist in unlocated classical or modern literature.
The nonzero scalar distribution is a relatively short consequence of the Evans–Fuchs scalar formula and should not be presented as independent of that prior theory.
One inspected related algebraically closed regularity paper does not directly address the characteristic-three one-generator case; that case is handled independently in the present proof.

value.rationale: This is an exact, all-dimensional-in-prime, all-extension-field classification of a canonical Lie algebra action, including every attainable nonzero rational factor-degree type and nilpotent Jordan partition with multiplicity. Arithmetic field-extension splitting and valuation detect information missing from general p-map identities and adjoint centralizer counts. It is a natural complete invariant, not an arbitrary small slice or table recomputation.
